name: Mohawk Electrical Systems Inc.
old_description: Mohawk Electrical Systems, Inc was founded by Clarence and Stephen Welch in 1963. In 1988, current president Scott Welch joined the company and became the third-generation owner in 2006.
about:
Mohawk Electrical Systems, Inc. is headquartered in Milford, Delaware. The company was founded in 1963 by Clarence and Stephen Welch. In 1988, Scott Welch joined the firm and became the third-generation owner in 2006, continuing family ownership.

The company operates as a basic-to-complex assembly integrator, combining precision manufacturing with quality components to produce custom assemblies. Core capabilities include bridgewire and ordnance products, electromechanical assemblies, cable and harness assemblies, and contract manufacturing. Processes encompass multi-conductor instrument cable, coaxial cable, specialty power cables, multi-point harnesses, and molded rubber components for turnkey assemblies.

Mohawk serves the defense, oil and gas, pyrotechnics, instrumentation, mining, and construction industries. Its products are used in military applications such as the M18A1 and M68 Claymore weapon systems, as well as in commercial explosive products for coal mining, dam construction, roads, railways, and other large projects. The company also supports oil and gas well perforating and pyrotechnic systems.

Mohawk emphasizes a reputation for superior quality and reliability of detonators in military applications. Its quality assurance program includes receiving inspection of all materials, infrared and video inspection technology, statistical process control during production, 100% line and final product inspection, and packing and shipping inspection. The firm states that this integrated approach delivers improved product quality, on-time delivery, and overall customer satisfaction.

name: Moldgenix
old_description: Moldgenix specializes in delivering one-of-a-kind injection molding solutions that optimize performance and streamline production.
about:
Moldgenix operates from Trumbauersville, Pennsylvania. The company traces its roots to 1987, when the legacy of excellence and innovation was established. In a recent chapter, the business was rebranded under the ownership of Haartz Family Holdings, LLC, a family-owned holding company, with Thomas Houdeshell serving as president.

The firm provides end-to-end contract manufacturing for plastic injection molding, including mold construction, micro-molding, tooling, automation, machining, and production. Its FDA-registered facility holds ISO 13485:2016 certification and offers clean room manufacturing compliant with the same standard. Secondary operations cover overmolding, laser marking, laser bonding, milling, welding, and ultrasonic welding, while assembly, kitting, and packaging services range from simple boxing to sealed medical packaging. The company handles both small-scale runs and full-scale production.

Moldgenix serves medical device OEMs, consumer product brands, personal care companies, and manufacturers in telecommunications, commercial, and high-end electronics markets. Its expertise spans Class I and II finished medical devices, jig and fixture construction, and finished goods packaging.

The company emphasizes a “Total Project Solution” from concept to completion, backed by over thirty years of packaging experience and a scientific injection molding approach. Its quality management system and clean room capabilities are positioned to meet rigorous medical and specialty market requirements.

name: Molding Dynamics Inc.
old_description: Our customers in many industries across the United States and around the world have come to us since 2001 for plastic injection molding solutions that exceed their expectations. Our highly skilled and experienced professionals specialize in engineering grade resins for parts that meet your requirements through an array of plastic
about:
Molding Dynamics Inc. was founded in 2001 in Bedford, Ohio, a suburb of Cleveland. The company began as a specialist in plastic injection molding using engineering-grade resins and has grown through acquisition and facility consolidation.

Today the company operates a 40,000-square-foot manufacturing facility housing 22 injection molding presses ranging from 75‑ton to 700‑ton capacity, including vertical presses with shuttle tables for complex insert molding. Its core processes cover custom plastic injection molding, insert molding, and overmolding, supported by value‑added services such as assembly, sonic welding, pad printing, chrome plating, and tooling transfers. The shop handles projects from short‑run prototypes to high‑volume production runs.

Molding Dynamics serves customers in energy (coal, fracking, wind, solar), consumer goods, medical, construction, and general industrial markets. The firm emphasizes tight‑tolerance components for medical devices, durable parts for construction and energy applications, and visually appealing pieces for consumer products.

The company differentiates itself through ISO‑compliant quality systems, early collaboration on design for manufacturing and material selection, a skilled workforce trained in‑house, and a reshoring program that promises reduced lead times, lower logistics costs, and tariff‑free domestic production.

about:
Molding Technologies LLC, doing business as Persistent Molding Technologies, operates from Versailles, Kentucky.

The company manufactures continuous-thread (CT) plastic caps in a range of standard sizes—including 20-410, 24-410, 28-410, and larger 89-400 configurations—and offers them in colors such as black, white, red, blue, and yellow. Beyond caps, it provides fluidized cleaning services for components and parts, repairs hot runner systems (both valve-gated and hot-tip designs), and delivers mold design services that span from initial part concept through pilot and production mold builds. Bulk ordering is available for cap products.

Its cap line serves food, beverage, beauty and personal care, healthcare, homecare, industrial, and nutraceutical markets, as well as industrial products and chemicals. The fluidized cleaning and hot runner repair services target manufacturers needing maintenance or cleaning of mold components.

Persistent Molding Technologies positions itself as a single source for molding-related needs, combining cap production, mold design, hot runner repair, and fluidized cleaning under one roof.

name: Montana Food Equipment
old_description: Discover top-tier kitchen equipment for gourmet cooking and lasting quality.
about:
Montana Food Equipment is a family-owned business based in Helena, Montana, founded in 1923 as Hobart Sales and Service. The company was purchased by the Caissey family in 1991, and Levi Caissey assumed ownership in 2010, running it with his wife Kristin. It operates from a 10,000-square-foot warehouse and a 6,000-square-foot showroom on Airport Road.

The company sells and services residential and commercial kitchen equipment, offering installation, maintenance, repair, and warranty work. Its 17-person staff includes technicians certified by the Commercial Food Equipment Service Association (CFESA) and trained by the EPA under Section 608 for refrigerant handling. The showroom displays functioning models from brands such as Hobart, BlueStar, True, Wolf, Sub-Zero, Cove, and Forno Bravo.

Commercial customers include grocery stores, delis, bakeries, meat shops, restaurants, schools, hospitals, and convenience stores across Montana and northern Idaho. Residential clients are home chefs seeking professional-grade appliances.

Montana Food Equipment emphasizes durable equipment and responsive service, citing a 24- to 48-hour standard response window and 12- to 24-hour emergency response. The company highlights its century-long local presence and factory-trained technicians as key differentiators.

name: Montana Metal Fabrications
old_description: Are you ready to grow with an amazing company with a unique job experience? We  are millwrights that cover the state of MT with installation, repairs and services to fertilizer, grain, seed, and feed elevators. We also do custom fabrication of almost anything  from small ornamental items to trailers. Employees will utilize and learn a wide range of skills and knowledge while working alongside both the company owners and co-workers.
about:
Montana Metal Fabrications, Inc. opened in Great Falls, Montana, on January 6, 2003. Founder Dean Brandt started the company to serve the state's grain, fertilizer, feed, and seed elevator operators with repair, installation, and custom parts fabrication. In 2010 Phil Gates joined the crew, and when Brandt retired in 2026, Gates and his wife Laura became the owners. The business remains privately held and operates mobile units that travel across Montana for on‑site work.

The company runs a full fabrication shop equipped for shearing, braking, and rolling 1/4‑inch steel, plus hand plasma cutters and a bending/rolling machine added in 2009 for ornamental scrolls, baskets, and pickets. Core output includes elevator components such as spouting, conveyors, legs, and distributors; custom utility trailers, flatbeds, and truck boxes; water, waste‑oil, and fuel tanks (up to 100 gallons); and a range of decorative items from fire pits and benches to BBQ smokers and custom art. Welding and repair cover carbon steel, stainless steel, and aluminum.

Primary customers are agricultural operations — commercial and private grain elevators, fertilizer plants, and feed/seed facilities — throughout Montana. The shop also serves industrial clients needing tower installations, ladders, catwalks, and drilling‑rig accessories, as well as residential buyers seeking one‑off ornamental metalwork.

The founders’ original goal was to keep Montana’s agricultural infrastructure running with reliable, local service. Today the team emphasizes versatility: “if you can dream it, we can probably build it,” backing that claim with mobile repair crews and a shop that handles both heavy structural work and fine decorative detail.

name: Montana Metalworks and Signs
old_description: The shop's welders bring years of hands-on experience across a wide range of completed project types, from intricate CNC signage to structural steel assemblies. That depth of skill translates into confident problem-solving, whether you're dealing with a broken piece of machinery in the field or planning a complex custom fabrication from scratch. Accountability and follow-through define how the work gets done.
about:
Montana Metal Works & Signs operates from Great Falls, Montana, as a locally owned and operated metal fabrication and welding shop serving Great Falls, Shelby, Fairfield, and the surrounding region. The company does not disclose a founding year or founder names, but presents itself as a direct-source fabricator with no subcontracting of metalwork.

The shop provides welding (including precision TIG for aluminum and stainless steel), custom metal fabrication, structural steel assemblies, CNC sign fabrication, sandblasting, and powder coating. All cutting, welding, and finishing are performed in-house using CNC cutting equipment, a powder coating system, and mobile welding rigs that allow on-site repairs across rural Montana. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are published.

Customers span residential, commercial, and agricultural sectors. Examples include ranchers needing custom gates and urgent equipment repairs, commercial property owners requiring railings and structural steel, and homeowners seeking custom signage and decorative metalwork. The company notes that agricultural repairs often demand quick turnaround to minimize operational impact, while architectural pieces require attention to design detail and finish quality.

The business emphasizes accountability, follow-through, and direct communication with the welders and fabricators doing the work. Its differentiators include complete in-house control from design through finish, mobile welding that brings full capabilities to the field, and after-hours emergency service. The team cites familiarity with Montana’s temperature swings, weather exposure, and agricultural schedules as context that shapes their approach to durability and scheduling.

name: Montana Milling
old_description: Our mix plant provides a large variety of mixes and blends for the baking industry.
about:
Montana Milling, Inc. operates grain mills in Conrad and Great Falls, Montana, in the heart of the state's Golden Triangle wheat-growing region. The company was founded in 1972 and has served the baking industry for over five decades.

The company specializes in custom milling, cleaning, flaking, cracking, and blending of more than 20 whole grains. Its product line includes hard red spring and winter wheat, hard white wheat, soft white wheat, barley (whole, dehulled, pearled, malted, hulless waxy), buckwheat, oat groats, steel-cut oats, millet, corn, flax, rye, triticale, spelt, kamut, durum, and peas. A dedicated mix plant produces custom flour blends, flakes, cracks, and specialty mixes to customer specifications. Every shipment undergoes personal quality checks before leaving the mill.

Primary customers are commercial bakeries and food manufacturers that require consistent, high-quality grain ingredients. Montana Milling also works directly with growers and owner-operators in the Golden Triangle to source certified organic and conventional crops.

The company emphasizes its location in a grain-producing area, its ability to tailor milling and blending to exact specifications, and a quality guarantee that includes strict testing standards and individual shipment inspection.

name: Monterey Company
old_description: Manufacturing custom promotional products for organizations worldwide since 1989.
about:
The Monterey Company operates from Bend, Oregon, where it has manufactured custom promotional products since 1989. The business began with a focus on challenge coins and patches for military and public‑safety organizations and has since expanded into a broad catalog of branded merchandise.

The company produces challenge coins (die‑struck, 3D, enamel), patches (embroidered, PVC, woven, leather, chenille, sublimated), enamel pins (hard/soft enamel, cloisonné, die‑struck), custom hats (Richardson, flexfit, snapback with embroidery or patch application), race medals, metal emblems, keychains, ornaments, charms, and a range of promotional items. Decoration processes include die striking, enamel filling, embroidery, PVC molding, laser etching, and sublimation. Minimum orders start at 25 pieces, with volume discounts on larger runs; the catalog lists thousands of SKUs.

Customers span the U.S. military (Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, National Guard), law enforcement, fire departments, corporate brands, and event organizers. Recent projects include challenge coins for the Indiana Army National Guard, custom belt buckles, embroidered patches for a firefighter apparel brand, and race medals for sporting events. The company also supplies nursing pins, letterman patches, and general promotional products such as apparel, magnets, and lanyards.

The Monterey Company emphasizes low minimums (25 pieces), free art proofs with unlimited revisions, a 2‑4 week standard turnaround, dedicated one‑on‑one account representatives, free domestic shipping, international shipping capability, pre‑production samples on request, and waived setup fees on exact reorders.

name: Moody Mountain Solar
old_description: Solar Installation Throughout Midcoast Maine and the Islands of Penobscot Bay.
about:
Moody Mountain Solar operates from Searsmont, Maine, and was founded in the spring of 2020 by Cory Alexander. After 15 years in the boat-building industry and a lifetime of off-grid living at sea and on land, Alexander started the company to deliver a more personalized solar design and installation experience. The business remains owner-operated, with Alexander serving as the NABCEP-certified system designer and the single point of contact for every project.

The company installs rooftop arrays, ground-mount systems, and off-grid power solutions across Midcoast Maine and the islands of Penobscot Bay. Its rooftop work emphasizes roof integrity, drawing on building-trades experience to ensure watertight mounts on asphalt, metal, and EPDM surfaces. Ground-mount installations incorporate bifacial panels, while off-grid systems use modern lithium battery storage. Alexander is on site for the full installation, and the firm handles design, permitting, and commissioning in-house.

Customers include homeowners seeking grid-tied systems, seasonal camps replacing generators, and island properties requiring micro-grid independence. The service area covers coastal towns and remote islands where utility access is limited or unreliable.

Alexander founded Moody Mountain Solar to offer premium service at a reasonable cost while maintaining a neighborly, community-focused approach. The company differentiates itself by keeping the designer on the job site, providing a single contact from quote to commissioning, and applying marine-grade attention to detail to every roof penetration.
